page: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 32 physical cores via hyperthreading. Hardware-assisted capabilities include AVX-512 extensions and AES cryptography acceleration. The architecture is configured with an extensive 1792.0 GB of system memory, providing 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is bundled with 7697 GB of integrated local SSD storage. No discrete graphics hardware accelerators are present.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate an architecture engineered predominantly for memory density and multi-threaded throughput rather than per-core compute speed. While single-threaded tests such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression register in the bottom decile, multi-core benchmarks show stable middle-tier performance, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score of 43,783.83 and 39.98 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Memory throughput reaches 182.37 GB/s for large uncached block reads and 73.3 GB/s for writes.

From an efficiency perspective, the platform trades peak single-thread execution efficiency for extreme memory capacity per core and large local scratch space. Workloads with heavy single-thread processing dependencies or intensive token-generation requirements will see limited returns. Instead, the hardware composition is appropriate for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching layers, relational database servers, and high-footprint analytical workloads requiring substantial memory residency.
description: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 1792.0 GB of RAM, yielding 28.0 GB of memory per vCPU, alongside 7697 GB of local SSD storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-threaded execution and robust memory bandwidth, evidenced by 39.98 million Redis SET operations per second and consistent multi-core stress testing, contrasted by poor single-threaded metrics. The instance provides a cost-effective density profile for infrastructure that requires vast physical memory capacity and high concurrent thread counts over raw per-core execution speeds. It is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large caching layers, relational database management systems, and heavy memory-bound analytics pipelines.
